What al{{ls}}o, to get perfection, 28. and what reward they {{ls}}hal haue that leaue al, yea or any part, for his {{ls}}ake. 31. he foretelleth of his Pa{{ls}}sion mo{{ls}}t particularly, 33. and entring into Iericho, cureth one blinde man.''}} {{dropinitial|A|fl={{verse|chapter=18|verse=1}}}}ND he {{ls}}pake al{{ls}}o a parable to them that it behoueth {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=∷ We {{ls}}hould pray alwaies by faith, hope, and charitie, and by working the thinges that be acceptable to God: though {{ls}}pecial times of vocal praiers in the Canonical houres be a{{ls}}{{ls}}igned for the {{ls}}turring of vs vp to God through external {{ls}}ignes of deuotion.}}∷ alwaies to pray, & not to be weary, {{verse|chapter=18|verse=2}}† {{ls}}aying, There was a certaine iudge in a certaine citie, vvhich feared not God, and of man made no accoumpt. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=3}}† And there vvas a certaine widow in that citie: and {{ls}}he came to him, {{ls}}aying, Reuenge me of mine aduer{{ls}}arie. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=4}}† And he vvould not of a long time. but aftervvard he {{ls}}aid vvithin him {{ls}}elf, Although I feare not God, nor make accoumpt of man: {{verse|chapter=18|verse=5}}† yet becau{{ls}}e this vvidovv is importune vpon me, I wil reuenge her, le{{ls}}t at the la{{ls}}t {{ls}}he come and defame me. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=6}}† And our Lord {{ls}}aid, Heare vvhat the iudge of iniquitie {{ls}}ayeth. {{verse|chapter=18|verse=7}}† And vvil not God reuenge his elect that crie to him day and night: and vvil he haue patience in them? {{verse|chapter=18|verse=8}}† I {{ls}}ay to you that he vvil quickly reuenge them. But yet the Sonne of man comming, {{sup|‖}} {{ls}}hal he finde trovv you, faith in the earth?
